ANALYSIS: Congenital Rubella Infection is a serious, potentially devastating condition caused by maternal rubella virus infection during pregnancy, leading to fetal damage — classic triad includes sensorineural deafness, cataracts, and congenital heart disease (e.g., PDA, pulmonary artery stenosis), along with other systemic manifestations (thrombocytopenia, hepatitis, encephalitis, developmental delay). A "Healthy newborn" implies absence of disease, abnormality, or sequelae — which is fundamentally incompatible with the diagnosis of congenital rubella infection, even in subclinical cases (which are rare and still involve viral persistence and potential late complications).
